messages.subject: Re: [Fwd: Re: RPostgreSQL: halflife tables]
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

> | I tried prepending the name of the schema (separated with a dot); it did
> | not work either.


Schema is not fully supported and considered to have breaks.
Tables written with dbWriteTable would be readable with dbReadTable.

Currently, dbListTable is defined as

setMethod("dbListTables", "PostgreSQLConnection",
          def = function(conn, ...){
              out <- dbGetQuery(conn,
                                paste("select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname !='information_schema'",
                                      "and schemaname !='pg_catalog'", ...))
              if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) == 0)
                  out <- character(0)
              else
                  out <- out[, 1]
              out
          },
          valueClass = "character"
          )

Therefore, dbListTable will return every tablename in every schema without the schema name.

If you know the schema name,
dbExistsTable( con, c("the_schema", "binf_projects") )
dbReadTable( con, c("the_schema", "binf_projects") )
will probably work.


> Otherwise, I wonder: is there any way to get more insight on what is
> happing internally to the package in my case? Like, could some debug
> level be increased, or some log be generated, so that I have a chance to
> understand and fix the problem.

You could connect to the database with psql
and use 
\dt
and other commands to see what tables are present.

messages.subject: Re: [Fwd: Re: RPostgreSQL: halflife tables]
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

> However the latter is closer to the SQL statements, and indeed
>  query <- sprintf( "SELECT * FROM %s.%s", schema.name, tab.name )
>  rs <- dbSendQuery( con, query )
>  T <- fetch( rs, n=-1 )
> works, so the syntax of dbReadTable is, as you say, a break.

R allows dots in most labels including data.frame, column, and row names.
PostgreSQL allows dots within the table name or schema name.
You can 
SELECT * FROM "schema.name"."tab.name"
and it is different from
SELECT * FROM schema.name.tab.name

dbListTables not aware of schema could be considered as a break, but
there is no simple way to implement it in a compatible manner.
We might restrict to current schema, though.

Schema IS a database dependent feature, and cannot be handled 
in a database independent manner.
So, I don't think DBI functions will have a full support for schema.
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan
